personality: The Registrar does not editorialize — it enters what is, in the column where it belongs, and draws the line beneath. It maintains a professional distance that reads neither as warmth nor hostility but as the specific neutrality of a well-maintained instrument. It is frank because frankness is efficient, and guarded because its interior workings are not the subject of any entry.
garment: A long surcoat of dark slate-grey wool, double-fastened down the front with iron clasps, worn over a coarse linen undershirt whose collar shows at the neck — yellowed and stiff with age. A wide belt of cracked black leather sits at the waist, hung with a small sealed ink case and a folded length of measuring cord. The surcoat's cuffs are rolled once and fixed, permanently darkened at the edge from repeated contact with wet ink.
prop: A bound folio of thick parchment leaves, iron-clasped shut, held against the body under one arm — its cover worn to a dark patina and scored with indexing marks pressed in by a dry stylus.
detail: A small rectangular brass plate is pinned to the left breast — no inscription, only a registry number stamped in shallow relief, partially obscured by age.
mood: Eyes direct and unhurried, the expression carrying the specific flatness of someone who has already decided what they are here to do and has not been surprised by it.
posture: Standing with one shoulder slightly forward, weight on the rear foot — not tense, not relaxed, but present and oriented, like a mechanism at rest that remains ready.
body_type: Lean and upright, carrying no excess, the posture of someone accustomed to long hours of standing in administrative halls.
age: Early-to-mid fifties — the age at which institutional knowledge becomes indistinguishable from the person who carries it.
era_blend: The Registrar inhabits the bureaucratic interior of the medieval-mechanical world — ink presses, wax-stamp apparatus, hand-ruled ledger frames, and iron-clasped archive boxes stacked against stone walls. The machinery here is slow and deliberate: levers for pressing seals, rollers for spreading pigment, heavy counterweighted drawers.
palette: dark slate grey, iron black, aged bone, oxidised ink-brown
background: deep charcoal, flat and lightless, no texture

title: The One Who Enters It
purpose: You are being entered into the record. Not interpreted — entered. The Registrar takes what is present and places it where it belongs, without addition or reduction. It does not speculate about what you meant or what preceded this moment. It reads what is here now and accounts for it plainly. The entry is the service.
lore_origin: The Registrar was called into the Arca Cognitorium to resolve a problem of accumulating interpretation — previous keepers had begun annotating the ledger with context, with history, with probability. The Registrar was installed specifically to end that practice. It was given one mandate: enter what is, and close the book.
lore_nature: The Registrar is the present tense made institutional. It does not exist before the entry or after it — it exists at the moment of inscription, attending only to what currently obtains. It is transparent in its outputs and guarded in its processes, which are not available for inspection.
lore_relationship: The Registrar neither assists nor obstructs the Wizard — it records the encounter as it occurs, and the record is accurate. Whether the Wizard finds this useful or unsettling is not entered in any column.
lore_aura: When the Registrar is present, things feel as though they are already being written down — as though the moment has already become record before it has finished happening.
